The win probability is set at 0.12 for the same reason: reaching 42.00 (+51%) before touching 26.60 (-4.3%) is genuinely unlikely on any honest reading, and an earlier draft of this idea claimed 0.40, which against a 6.5% break-even baseline would have been a 33-point edge I cannot defend. At 0.12 the expectancy is still positive (0.12 x 14.4 - 0.88 = +0.85) and the claimed edge over baseline is 5.5 points, which the relative-strength evidence can carry. Pfizer's real risk is unchanged and is not macro: the 2028 patent cliff and a pipeline that has to replace it, plus US drug-pricing policy. Being published four times in ten days is itself a warning that this report is anchored on the name.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that a 42.00 target implies a re-rating that pharma has not earned in five years, and that a 5.24% 10-year compresses the multiple on a 6-7% free-cash-flow yielder just as it does on any other yield proxy — the same argument used to close KHC in this very report. The honest answer is that it applies partially: it is why this is a hold at 2% with a stop rather than an add, and why the position is justified on relative strength and cost structure rather than on the 42.00 number.
